parsed.summary: This paper proposes a unified energy decomposition framework for self-supervised visual representation learning based on three non-overlapping principles: observation, prediction, and regularization. By pre-training a ViT-Tiny encoder on STL-10, the authors demonstrate that all three principles are necessary to prevent collapse and learn high-quality semantic and spatial representations.

chk_problem.value: Understanding the necessary principles for self-supervised visual representation learning and preventing representational collapse.
chk_problem.paper_quote: We argue that learning visual representations without labels requires a training signal jointly complete across three non-overlapping objectives: semantic invariance across augmented views, patch-level spatial prediction, and representational non-degeneracy.

chk_method.value: A unified energy decomposition framework that instantiates three jointly trained objectives: invariance (observation), predictive (prediction), and regularization.
chk_method.paper_quote: We instantiate Equation (3) as three jointly trained objectives, Ltotal = αLinv + βLpred + γLreg .

chk_data.value: The unlabeled split of the STL-10 dataset.
chk_data.paper_quote: We pre-train a ViT-Tiny encoder (embedding dimension 192, depth 12, patch size 8) on the unlabeled split of STL-10 [12] at 96×96, giving 144 patch tokens.

chk_setup.value: Pre-training a ViT-Tiny encoder on STL-10 for 200 epochs using AdamW, evaluated via linear probing and patch-level retrieval.
chk_setup.paper_quote: We train 200 epochs with AdamW, batch size 512, and a cosine-decayed peak learning rate 5×10−4 , evaluating by linear probe and patch-level retrieval (Section 6).

chk_primary_result.value: The full contrastive model with SIGReg achieves 55.0% linear probe accuracy, while removing regularization, prediction, or observation drops accuracy to 51.6%, 49.5%, and 41.6% respectively.
chk_primary_result.paper_quote: Against our proposed model (row J, 55.0%), removing regularization (row H) costs 3.4 points, removing prediction (row F) 5.5 points, and removing observation (row E) 13.4 points, the largest single drop.

chk_secondary_result.value: Removing prediction causes a 3.1-point drop in spatial recall@5 for patch-level nearest-neighbour retrieval, confirming its role in learning spatial structure.
chk_secondary_result.paper_quote: Removing prediction (row F) causes a 3.1-point drop in spatial recall@5 relative to the full model (row J), directly confirming the structural argument of Proposition 10: without a spatial training signal the encoder does not learn to distinguish patch positions.

chk_baseline.value: Strict subsets of the three principles (omitting one or more of invariance, prediction, or regularization) and prior self-supervised methods.
chk_baseline.paper_quote: Each row instantiates a strict subset of {Linv , Lpred , Lreg }, verifying Propositions 7, 10, and 11 and Theorem 8 and Remark 9.

chk_conclusion.value: Self-supervised representation learning can be unified and successfully trained using three modular, non-overlapping principles: observation, prediction, and regularization, without relying on implicit collapse-prevention mechanisms.
chk_conclusion.paper_quote: We formalized self-supervised representation learning as energy minimization over three non-overlapping principles: observation, prediction, and regularization.

chk_limitation.value: The empirical validation is limited to a single small scale (ViT-Tiny on STL-10), leaving open whether these findings scale to larger models.
chk_limitation.paper_quote: Our empirical validation is at a single small scale (Section 6); whether a larger encoder could acquire spatial structure from observation alone, or cross-view invariance from prediction alone, remains open.
